chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu al-Maghra', from al-Halabi, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who sells an animal in 'usfa' (sale by description) with known teeth and known color, then is given less than the agreed condition or more than it; he said: 'If it is with the pleasure/contentment of your soul and his soul, then there is no harm.'

key_terms.أَسْنَانٍ: Teeth, used here as a key indicator of an animal's age and quality.
key_terms.شَرْطِهِ: The agreed condition or specification of the sale.
key_terms.طِيبَةِ نَفْسٍ: Contentment or pleasure of the soul, indicating mutual consent to the terms.
key_terms.وُصَفَاءَ: Sale by description (usfa), where goods are sold based on known characteristics rather than immediate inspection.

ai.seo_question: Is a sale valid if the delivered item differs slightly from its description, provided both parties are satisfied?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that in sales by description (bay' al-mawsuf), the validity hinges on mutual consent (rida) rather than strict adherence to the initial specification, provided the deviation is not deceptive. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) emphasizes that if both buyer and seller are pleased with the outcome—whether the delivered item is slightly less or more than described—the transaction remains sound. This reflects the Shia juristic principle that *rida* (contentment) can cure minor defects in description, distinguishing it from cases of significant uncertainty (gharar).
